thread.title: Tech Today: Facebook’s Fall, AMD’s New High, an Apple Beat? - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Facebook’s Fall, AMD’s New High, an Apple Beat? - Barron's
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated July 26, 2018 3:08 p.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech:
Facebook’s Fall
Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are down $43.18, or 19%, to $174.32, continuing last night’s after-hours collapse, and headed toward its highest close in over a decade, after the company yesterday afternoon missed analysts’ revenue expectations for its Q2 , failed to meet the expectations for growth in its users, and said its revenue growth is set to plummet this quarter and next, and that its profit margins will deteriorate sharply over the next several years.
The stock is now facing something of a credibility gap for CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his team from analysts for having failed to warn them about the big change in the outlook for growth and profit.
My colleague Jonathan Schwartz explores whether there is now more reason for a subscription -based offering of Facebook, based on the views of Macquarie Research ’s Ben Schachter , who thinks there’s never been a better time for it.
AMD Headed to 11-Year High
Shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) are up $2.30, or 14%, to $18.35, steadily adding gains today after the company yesterday afternoon beat with its Q2 results, though it forecast revenue this quarter below consensus.
At this rate, the stock is on course for its highest close since Jan. 18, 2007 —$17.92, according to Dow Jones's data gurus.
CEO Lisa Su , in my interview with her this morning , said the company is focused on taking share from Intel ( INTC ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) in the data center server chip market, as the company’s “number one priority."
Qualcomm Surges After Abandoning NXP
Shares of chip giant Qualcomm ( QCOM ) shares are up $3.63, or 6%, to $63.05, after t he company yesterday afternoon said it would give up on a $52 billion bid to acquire NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), and instead pursue up to $30 billion worth of stock buybacks.
Price targets are zooming at several shops, though the concern remains on the part of some that this company won’t be able to diversify now that it won’t be buying NXP.
For the bulls, Mike Walkley of Canaccord Genuity reiterates a Buy rating, and raises his target to $81 from $75, writing that "ending the uncertainty of buying NXP is positive” for the stock. He also sees "strong earnings growth over the next several years due to the increased share-repurchase program.”
And he thinks it’s likely the company will settle disputes with Apple ( AAPL ) and with Huawei .
That would let the company focus on the “long-term opportunity” of 5G wireless.
For the bears, Stifel Nicolaus ’s Kevin Cassidy reiterates a Hold rating, and raises his target to $58 from $54, wiring that he “appreciates” the "earnings accretion” of the buyback plan, "but Qualcomm’s long-term product strategy returns to its core mobile business,” something he’s not as thrilled with.
As for NXP, its stock today is down $5.23, or 5%, to $93.14, even thought it gets a $2 billion breakup fee from Qualcomm.
Nice Trends for Apple
Speaking of Apple, which reports fiscal Q3 results next Tuesday, Aug. 31, some observers are getting mildly excited.
Ken Berman , a columnist with Kiplinger’s and Forbes , offers that Apple will beat big time, with perhaps $1 billion above the consensus $53 billion revenue estimate for the quarter, and perhaps 7 cents above the average $2.26 estimate.
His reasoning is there will be a “heavier mix of higher-priced iPhones, momentum on the iPad side of the business and strength in services."
Berman thinks that means Apple will see a jump following the report of "more than 6% from current levels, pushing the company past the vaunted $1 trillion valuation ."
And Jun Zhang with Rosenblatt thinks that while the fiscal Q3 report is going to be merely in line with expectations, there’s prospect for upside in the outlook.
"We believe Apple will move production for its newest LCD model to mid-August, up from September,” writes Zhang, "leading to Apple giving in-line or stronger than consensus guidance for FQ4 ($59.4 billion & $2.65)."
Apple today is down 14 cents to $194.68.
Micron Rises on Hynix Perspective
Shares of DRAM chip maker Micron Technology ( MU ) are up 53 cents, or 1%, to $53.93, after DRAM competitor SK Hynix ( 000660KS ) overnight reported results that shine a favorable light on DRAM.
As Vijay Rakesh with Mizuho notes, Hynix suggested there are DRAM shortages , and demand is healthy.
"There have been concerns with some potential China server demand and inventory but Hynix noted it does NOT see any Server DRAM demand or inventory issues in China,” writes Rakesh.
"Hynix also noted China Server OEMs are asking for pull in of DRAM orders in 3Q/4Q and seeing upside DRAM demand to its LTA [long-term agreements]."
Can Amazon Shine?
On tap for this afternoon, after the closing bell, another super-earnings afternoon. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) reports, along with Intel, and a host of others: 8x8 ( EGHT ), Atlassian ( TEAM ), Cypress Semiconductor ( CY ), Electronic Arts ( EA ), Maxim Integrated Products ( MXIM ), MicroStrategy ( MSTR ), Verisign and ( VRSN ) .
Amazon shares are trading lower in advance, down $49.64, or 2.7%, to $1,813.97.
